curriculum.lesson_evidence: Word choice carries denotation (dictionary meaning) and connotation (associated feeling). Swapping synonyms can shift tone from neutral to hostile or tender. Test replacements in the line.

lesson.child_mission: Word choice carries denotation (dictionary meaning) and connotation (associated feeling). Swapping synonyms can shift tone from neutral to hostile or tender. Test replacements in the line.
lesson.evidence_instructions: Save the independent response, specific revisions and both short-answer explanations; record oral evidence for speaking tasks.
lesson.extension: Apply the same strategy to an unfamiliar topic or audience, then compare the effect of two different choices.
lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Replace 'said' and 'walked' in a two-line draft with choices that shift tone; explain connotations.

FEEDBACK
Strong answer: New verbs shift feeling (e.g. muttered/stormed) with brief connotation notes.

CHECK
Thinking all synonyms are interchangeable. Connotation changes tone.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Revise a stanza for connotation: produce a tone chart of six swapped words and a final version.

Write a short reflection describing one specific revision you made and why.
lesson.learning_intention: Word choice carries denotation (dictionary meaning) and connotation (associated feeling). Swapping synonyms can shift tone from neutral to hostile or tender. Test replacements in the line.
lesson.offline_alternative: Use paper and pencil to complete the original task, then retain a photograph or short parent observation as evidence.

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
'House' versus 'home' versus 'dump' share possible denotations of dwelling but different connotations. In a poem about leaving, 'home' may ache more than 'house'.

TRY FIRST
Replace 'said' and 'walked' in a two-line draft with choices that shift tone; explain connotations.

FEEDBACK
Strong answer: New verbs shift feeling (e.g. muttered/stormed) with brief connotation notes.
teach_steps.explain:
Word choice carries denotation (dictionary meaning) and connotation (associated feeling). Swapping synonyms can shift tone from neutral to hostile or tender. Test replacements in the line.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make decisions based on specific language evidence, rather than guess or copy someone else. Keep the meaning accurate and explain the choice.

HOW TO WORK
Read the original example and locate the words or actions that support the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Check your response against the feedback: did you address the same skill and show your reasoning? If a detail is uncertain, identify what would have to be checked. One deliberate, justified revision is more useful than making the answer longer.
teach_steps.notice: Thinking all synonyms are interchangeable. Connotation changes tone. Correct the meaning, not just the appearance.
